vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: icp-filing
Version: 2.3.5

The skill bundle provides informational resources and utility commands for navigating the ICP filing process in China. The scripts (icp.sh and script.sh) are straightforward tools for generating checklists, process flows, and HTML footer snippets, or managing a local log file in ~/.local/share/icp-filing/. No evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or prompt injection was found.

llm.summary: The skill's files and runtime instructions align with an ICP-filing CLI/guide: it contains local scripts that generate checklists, process flows, and write data to a local data directory; it does not request credentials or call remote endpoints.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (ICP filing guide) matches the included files: a Bash CLI wrapper and a Python helper producing checklists, process steps, query guidance, province prefixes and footer HTML. There are no unrelated dependencies, cloud credentials, or surprising binaries.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the scripts instruct local CLI usage and explicitly reference an environment variable ICP_FILING_DIR to control the data directory. The SKILL.md does not declare required env vars formally, but the reference is benign (optional data-dir override). The runtime instructions do not ask the agent to read arbitrary system files, credentials, or to transmit data to external services.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is provided (instruction-only skill). The repository includes only local scripts (no downloads, no package installs). There is no remote fetch or archive extraction in the install path.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not require any credentials or secrets. The only environment variable referenced is ICP_FILING_DIR (optional) to set where local data/logs are stored; this is proportionate to a CLI tool that stores its own data.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The scripts create and write files under a per-user data directory (default: ~/.local/share/icp-filing) including data.log and history.log. This is expected for a CLI utility, but users should be aware the skill will write files to their home directory when run. The skill does not request elevated privileges nor persist as an always-enabled skill.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent with its stated purpose and contains only local CLI scripts that produce guidance and small local data files. Before installing or running: (1) review the scripts (they are short and readable) to confirm you are comfortable with them; (2) note that it will create a per-user data directory (default ~/.local/share/icp-filing) and write logs/data there—if you prefer a different location set the ICP_FILING_DIR environment variable; (3) do not run these scripts as root; (4) the skill does not require or send credentials or call external services, but if you modify the scripts to add network behavior re-audit them. Overall the skill is internally consistent and low-risk.
